neighbours.label: the first word of a reply that pushes back on or answers a quoted claim ('Yes, but', 'Actually', 'I also'); the same quoted claim followed by neutral narration stays quiet
fire: "Electric cars are useless in winter." Yes, but owners in Norway drive them all year.
"Nobody reads books anymore." Actually, library loans went up last year.
"Dogs can't see color." Yes, but they do see blue and yellow quite well.
"Vinyl sounds better than digital." Actually, most listeners cannot tell them apart.
"Coffee stunts your growth." Well, I drank it as a kid and I grew tall anyway.
"Remote work kills productivity." Yes, but our team shipped more since going remote.
"The museum is boring." Actually, I found the new wing fascinating.
"Running ruins your knees." We have heard that, but studies say otherwise.
quiet: "Electric cars are useless in winter." The headline ran in a local paper in January.
"Nobody reads books anymore." The poster hung by the door of the shop.
"Dogs can't see color." The quote appeared in a magazine article in 1998.
"Vinyl sounds better than digital." The slogan was printed on the store's bags.
"Coffee stunts your growth." The phrase was written on a sign at the diner.
"Remote work kills productivity." The title was chosen for the company newsletter.
"The museum is boring." The comment was posted on the review site last week.
"Running ruins your knees." The line was printed under a photo of a runner.

predictions: fire 0.15-0.4 on the reply word; near misses below 0.05
short: start of a reply to a quoted claim
notes: Card: Yo, Actually, my, that, but, I'd, We after a quoted or stated claim. Probe: 'Yes, but' after quoted claim 0.396, 'I also felt' 0.316, 'Actually,' 0.198, 'We could easily show' 0.140; same quoted claim + neutral narration 0.022, sentence without the claim 0.003, bare 'Actually is an adverb' 0.023. Weak pole on short probes.
